query: How does goal achievement vary across department, metric, and the management practices described?

per_column.name: goal_outcome_domain
per_column.rationale: Well-separated, interpretable categories (revenue_growth, cost_reduction, etc.) that segment goals by outcome type; a natural axis to compare achievement against, distinct from the raw metric column.

per_column.name: implementation_lever_type
per_column.rationale: Captures the management practice/lever used (process_automation, training_engagement, etc.), directly matching the query's focus on management practices; interpretable and groupable with reasonable spread.

per_column.name: metric_alignment_clarity
per_column.rationale: Ordinal-like clarity of metric alignment (aligned/misaligned/ambiguous). The 'ambiguous' cell is near-empty (1) but the aligned/misaligned split is meaningful and comparable against achievement.

per_column.name: stakeholder_engagement_signal
per_column.rationale: Binary management-practice indicator with a healthy split (349/201), enabling a clean grouped comparison of achievement by engagement presence.

per_column.name: time_horizon_category
per_column.rationale: Interpretable temporal segmentation (quarterly/fiscal_year/multi_year); multi_year is sparse but the two dominant buckets support meaningful comparison.

per_column.name: outcome_specificity
per_column.rationale: Ordinal goal-setting quality dimension (direction-only vs end-state vs milestone) with good spread; a classic management-practice axis to relate to achievement.

per_column.name: improvement_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categories of how improvement is pursued; partially overlaps with implementation_lever_type but is distinct enough and well-separated.

per_column.name: quantified_financial_impact
per_column.rationale: Binary flag on whether financial impact is quantified (388/162); interpretable practice signal that can be grouped against achievement.

judge.rationale: All eight added columns are external, associational, and interpretable segmentation variables aligned with the query's dimensions (outcome domain, management practices, metric alignment, time horizon, goal specificity). None merely restate goal_achievement, and none are opaque scores or fine-grained IDs. The set strongly supports discovering interpretable relationships. Minor deductions: some columns overlap semantically (implementation_lever_type vs improvement_mechanism), and a few categories are near-degenerate (ambiguous=1, multi_year=16), slightly limiting comparison in those buckets.
